self.title: What If Our Starting Assumptions Are Wrong?

detail.title: Assessing Epistemic Self-Correction Limits
detail.question: Can automated systems reliably identify and correct foundational methodological assumptions without external intervention?
detail.reason: Transitioning to synthesis after initiating targeted research on recursive self-correction architectures.

detail.title: Limitations of Automated Epistemic Self-Correction
detail.summary: While agentic frameworks like Popper [source-0c3114b8bfe140df] and Bayesian optimization [source-f0f5479363014d20] demonstrate significant advancements in automated hypothesis testing and system falsification, these systems operate within fixed methodological parameters. They do not demonstrate autonomous revision of their foundational epistemic assumptions, which remain subject to the external normative constraints identified in ethics-based auditing literature [source-f26a645e047847a2].
detail.reason: Revision based on new findings regarding Popper and Bayesian Optimization as specific falsification mechanisms distinct from broad epistemic self-correction.

detail.title: Limitations of Automated Epistemic Self-Correction
detail.summary: Analysis of automated decision-making and cognitive systems indicates that while algorithmic frameworks can process complex tasks, identifying and revising foundational methodological assumptions typically requires external oversight and normative evaluation.
detail.reason: Synthesizing available source material on automated decision-making and cognitive extension to address the project question.
